column3: NASB supplies “reigned.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Subject” is rendered “servant,” and “returned tribute” as “paid him tribute.”
“Treason” is rendered “conspiracy”; “arrested him … confined him” is rendered “shut him up and bound him.”
“Came up in all the land” is rendered “invaded the whole land.”
“Habor, the river of Gozan” is rendered “Habor, on the river of Gozan,” and “Media” as “the Medes.”
NASB supplies “this came about, because.”
“Which they had done” is rendered “which they had introduced.”
“Did secretly” translates an uncertain Hebrew verb; “cities” is rendered “towns.”
“Asherah poles” is rendered “Asherim,” and “luxuriant” as “green.”
“Made smoke” is rendered “burned incense.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew “by the hand of every prophet of his, every seer” is close; NASB supplies “His.”
“Trusted” is rendered “believe.”
“Testimonies” is rendered “warnings,” and “walked after” as “followed.”
“A molten image” is rendered “molten images,” and “Asherah pole” as “an Asherah.”
“Divined divinations and practiced divination” is rendered “practiced divination and enchantments.”
“From His face” is rendered “from His sight.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Offspring” is rendered “descendants.”
“Enticed away” follows the reading tradition (written text “drove away”); NASB renders “drove Israel away.”
The Hebrew “from it” is rendered “from them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “men.”
NASB supplies “therefore” and “some of.”
NASB supplies “they” for the impersonal subject.
The Hebrew plural “let them go and let them dwell” is rendered as singular (“let him go and live”).
Close to the Hebrew.
“Nation nation” is rendered “every nation,” and “Samaritans” as “the people of Samaria.”
Close to the Hebrew.
